packetText:
# Slide 9 — AI Can Personalize and Accelerate Microlearning

## Status

- current deck numbering: slide 9
- legacy source mapping: same as current
- decision state: OPEN

## Why this slide exists

- modernize the talk
- show a credible educational role for AI
- keep the conversation focused on pedagogy rather than hype

## Locked slide thesis

AI is most promising when it helps adapt cases, sequence review, and provide
targeted educational feedback.

## Slide purpose brief

- top claim:
  AI may improve personalization and timing
- support claim:
  the value is adaptive support around good educational design
- non-goals:
  - do not build a chatbot hero slide
  - do not imply autonomous education is the goal

## Figure job

- show targeted adaptation
- make AI feel like a quiet layer around the workflow
- keep the visual language premium and calm

## Locked copy

- header:
  `AI can personalize and accelerate microlearning.`
- subheader:
  `The emerging opportunity is adaptive support, not full automation.`
- figure labels:
  - `cases`
  - `feedback`
  - `timing`
  - `gaps`

## Visual rules

- no robots
- no futuristic command center
- no hype gradients or glowing neon AI clichés

## Existing useful source assets

- `inputs/microlearning_emergency_medicine_review.md`
- `inputs/saem_microlearning_talk_outline.md`

## Immediate next refinement

- test an adaptive-pathway composition
- compare a closed-loop learning system with a targeted-review map
